notes: A wholly handwritten English letter leaf, signed R. Hartshorne, with manuscript page number 2 and archive number 54. It has no date, address, salutation, or independent heading on this leaf. The cited page reference is p. 38. The writer says he believes the artinian hypothesis unnecessary under the stated AR-J-adic noetherian hypotheses, then gives an argument using three exact sequences and Artin-Rees. This is a report of what the page claims, not an independent validation of that argument. The quoted paper title is Affine Duality and Cofiniteness, enclosed by two raised strokes at each end. The leaf closes with a promise to send a copy, Sincerely yours, and the signature. The expressed author qualification is I believe; no author question mark was found. All four explicit C uncertainties are retained. The lower-case let after a full stop is preserved. H supplies a description only, so it is unavailable as a transcription and all h_reading fields are null with diff_h false. The unrelated trailing cover description accidentally present in the initial packet was disregarded. There are three exact-sequence rows and three thin upward arrows; their hand is not established. Six tight crops were each viewed once after the whole image and the two halves were each viewed once.
math_reading_decisions: The opening X and Z, the first-sequence X/Y/Z, and the hooked J forms have ordinary single strokes. The raised AR belongs before the first -J-adic and is retained as an insertion.
The first exponent n+1 before X is definite. The joined terminal strokes in the later two exponents leave the C n+1 versus n+{} alternative unresolved at its first occurrence, before Y.
Each lower n in the first equality is below the baseline. The final n in (A/J^{n+1})_n lies outside the closing parenthesis.
The limit has a separate continuous left-pointing arrow below lim.
The M terms carry zero, one, and two raised prime strokes as transcribed. The tensor signs have enclosing loops and internal crossing strokes.
The defined system A and the four A symbols paired with tensors have doubled left diagonals and are written as \mathbb{A}. The numerator A in the quotient has an ordinary single diagonal.
The category P has small AR below the baseline. The map to Y has two waves above a separate right-pointing arrow.
All twelve horizontal exact-sequence arrows point right. The three thinner arrows point upward from the bottom sequence to X, Y, and Z, crossing the middle row without terminating there.
